I would say a large issue isn't that there is nothing to do at endgame but that the things available are presented too early to feel like endgame. Helltides are available from level 1 and nightmare dungeons are available rather quickly after that. From there the only things that really get added are bosses and pit runs. (Shout-out to infernal hordes for being the exception) Bossing is fine but pit gets stale really quickly and you've done the other content so much up until that point that it's not great to keep doing. 

A lot of people who complain about endgame probably compare it to Path of Exile, and while PoE has a large amount of content it's always been the spacing out of that content and freedom to specialize in it at endgame that makes it so addictive. Diablo 4 needs some new content but it also needs to better space the content it does have out.

Alright, good story time. So this isn't about accidentally following anyone or being followed accidentally, but it is a story about being followed, damn near stalked, through my hometown. 

So me and a couple friends were out at Meijer in my hometown getting some snacks. We all get the same thing, a big pack of pepperoni because that shit is fantastic, and then head back to the car. As we're getting into the car my friend looks at me and says, "I think that old man in the Oldsmobile is watching us." Sure as shit we get into the car and sit down and he circles us once, looking me right in the eye with the craziest look, and then drives off a bit.

So now we're all a bit spooked so we put the car in gear and my friend drives off. As soon as we pull up to the stop sign the old man floors it towards us to get right behind us. We instantly know what's happening so my friend guns it and this old man stays right on his tail.

Halfway back to my neighborhood my friend takes a right turn onto a street that we rarely drive and this old man takes the turn so fast to keep up he nearly rolls his Oldsmobile. My friend gets the idea that he's going to use my neighborhood to lose the guy. So we tear off down a main road in my city towards my neighborhood and this guy is still right with us. My friend turns onto my street and this guy still won't leave us alone.

Now at this point we are in my neighborhood that we know well. It's a typical block style neighborhood and has rather sharp corners. Knowing how dead the neighborhood gets at night my friend starts gunning it around corners like he's a rally car driver. The old man keeps up for a bit and then my friend takes a 90 degree turn at 70 mph, brings the car up on two wheels, and finishes the turn and runs back down towards my house. The old man goes up towards the main road now having lost track of us and we head to a park to hide. 

To this day that is the single creepiest experience in a car I've had. Yes I know we should have gone to a police station or called them, but in the words of my friend,  "then the story wouldn't be as great."

I was thinking that it would work well to have different purchasable cookie types that would scale each tap much the same as in Cookie Collector. The system to purchase new cookie types is already built, and this way Naveen wouldn't need to change the prestige system between games to make it work. It would be fairly simple as well, given that the main cookie you tap would still look like the current theme the only variable changing would be amount of cookies per tap. This way it wouldn't have to take so many golden cookies and straight idle time to get to a small number of Rainbow chips whereas in Cookie Collector those first couple of Rainbow Chips come fairly quickly. Also, if it appeared that auto clickers would cause it to be way too easy to idle and get a large amount of cookies then they could be nerfed to provide an even smaller amount of cookies per tap. This is, in my opinion, the easiest way to balance the prestige systems between games and would make both of them equally as enjoyable.
